name: CI / CD | Reusable pipelines
tagline: GitHub Actions workflows and bash scripts reused across my projects, from Docker Swarm deployments to npm and browser store releases.

keyPoints: Single-project workflow: build and publish a Docker image to GitHub's registry, generate the stack file, deploy to Docker Swarm over SSH.
Multi-service workflow (client, server, migrations): staging then production, with images promoted from staging and a database backup restored if the deployment fails.
Health checks after each deployment, with automatic rollback to the previous stack.
Package workflows: npm publishing with provenance, browser extension packaging and store submissions behind manual approval.
Old images pruned from the registry and from the server.

popTagline: Written once, then reused and adapted from project to project.

overview.mainContent: Every project deploys with the same building blocks: job scripts running in GitHub Actions, and deployment scripts copied to the server and run over SSH. Stack files are generated from a template, so a project only declares its names, domain and ports.
keyPoints: Image tags injected into the generated stack file. Production reuses the tags validated in staging.
Pull requests to the main branch only from staging. The staging branch is recreated after each release.
Files of failed deployments archived with a timestamp.
Release guards: the tag must be on the main branch and match the package version.

purpose.title: Purpose
keyPoints: To deploy every project the same, predictable way.
To make a failed deployment a non-event: detected, rolled back, archived.

constraints.title: Constraints
keyPoints: Plain bash and GitHub Actions, no additional platform.
Secrets kept in GitHub and Docker secrets, never in the repository.
Readable by one person, months later.

choices.title: Promote, don't rebuild
choices.mainContent: Production deploys the exact images validated in staging, by copying their tags.

choices.title: Health checks, then rollback
choices.mainContent: After deploying, replica counts are polled. If services aren't healthy in time, the previous stack file is restored and deployed again.

choices.title: Scripts on both sides
choices.mainContent: Job scripts run on the CI runner, deployment scripts on the server: each side can also be run by hand.

challenges.title: Keeping copies in sync
challenges.mainContent: Reusing scripts by copying them means improvements have to be carried over by hand from one repository to another.

challenges.title: Keeping actions up to date
challenges.mainContent: GitHub retiring Node 20 for actions meant moving every workflow to newer action versions, and pinning the runner images.

keyPoints: A rollback path is what makes frequent deployments comfortable.
Conventions (service and stack names) are what make scripts reusable.
